title: People Making Over $100,000 Per Year are Acting Like They are Living Paycheck to Paycheck
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc uses a Dollar General management observation — that even households earning over $100,000 a year now shop like lower-income consumers, buying soap one bar at a time at a higher unit price instead of a 24-pack from Costco or Walmart — as evidence that consumers are living closer to paycheck to paycheck despite high incomes. That behaviour favours Dollar General, which typically thrives in difficult times. He traces the squeeze to tariffs in 2025 raising import costs, the 2026 war with Iran lifting oil prices and disrupting supply chains, and higher insurance and medical costs, on top of inflation since the 2020-21 stimulus era. Analysts have grown more optimistic on Dollar General since 2025 and now expect 11.4% EPS growth over the next several years; management guides operating margin to 6-8%, already improving from 4% to 5.6% through lower shrink/theft and store investment in long under-invested locations. At a forward PE of 15 the stock looks slightly overvalued to him for a low-single-digit revenue-growth industry, and he takes the under on analyst EPS forecasts, expecting 7-9% instead, doubting management executes the full turnaround. His updated DCF value is $165 versus a $126 market price. Call: DG — BUY (reiterated from 7 April, low conviction) — a buying opportunity he is not very confident in.
